The negative slope of the liquid–solid equilibrium line in water’s phase diagram occurs because ice (H2O(s)) is less dense than liquid water (H2O(l)).  
This unusual behavior arises from the hydrogen-bonded crystalline structure of ice, which holds water molecules farther apart on average than in the liquid state.  
That lower density means increasing pressure favors the liquid phase, shifting the melting point to lower temperatures as pressure rises — hence the negative slope.
